1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Sh. Narender Kumar Bindal vs Union Of India on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37672440/
1 Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land LAC no.
250/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Narender Kumar Bindal v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 11 with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

sentences.text: The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioner is the recorded owner/bhumidhar in possession of full share in the land bearing Khasra no. 46/1 min (007), 2 min (013) total admeasuring 1 Bigha 00 biswas situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.
It is stated that the petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.

LAC no. 250/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Narender Kumar Bindal v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 The actual physical possession of the said land is with the petitioner as the physical possession of the land has not been taken and the respondents shall take possession thereof from the petitioner.

entities.text: Narender Kumar Bindal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The LAC passed the award in a mechanical way without applying the mind and without going through the claim filed by the petitioner, as such the award is not acceptable to the petitioner, and she has received the awarded amount under protest and without prejudice to their rights.
The LAC failed to take note of the actual and practical market value of the said land and had adopted a narrow approach while observing that no proof of claim market value is attached.
The LAC has not assessed the actual market value of the said land in spite having knowledge of the fair market value adjudicated by the courts.

The LAC has failed to properly appreciate the quality, status,
potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

6. It is stated that the said land is well connected with the transport, telecommunication, roads and have all the basic amenities in and around the surrounding areas i.e. Mundka railway station is 1.5 kms away from the said land, Mundka Udyog Vihar Extension is located at a distance of about 2.5 kms away from the said land, where commercial activities are carried out and reputed clubs and party lawns are located within a radius of 24 kms away from the said land; godown of Food Corporation of India is at a distance of 3.5 kms away from the said land, District Sports School and the bottling plant of Indian Oil Corporation and Fortunes World's biggest 500 companies are at a distance of 3.5 - 4 kms away from the said land, NH10 LAC no. 250/2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW))
Narender Kumar Bindal v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 is at a distance of 2 kms away from the said land and Azad Hind Gram is at a distance of 4  5 kms away from the said land.

It is stated that the situation of the above stated areas shows the great importance in assessing the market value of the said land, and the similarly situated land was sold @ Rs. 2000/ per square yards by the vendors, therefore, the said land, which could easily fetch the same rate and the said land cannot be granted the market value less than Rs. 2000/ per sq. yards.
As such the ld. LAC has failed to take note of the judicial pronouncements and the government policy of 10% yearly escalation in the market value of the said land.
9. It is stated that the respondent no.2 has allotted the adjoining Rohini residential land to persons for residential as well as commercial LAC no. 250/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))

Union of India Page no. 5 of 11 purposes for more than Rs. 6000/ per square yards and that too, only to those who has applied for the plots/flats and shops well in advance, which fact shows that that the land for residential and commercial purposes was not easily available at the rate of Rs. 6000/ per square yards.

sentences.text: The respondent no.2 has been allotting the plots at the remotest and undeveloped the land, therefore, it is clear that the respondent no.2 cannot gain/earn profit at the cost of causing loss to the petitioner.
10. The ld. LAC, while passing the award has erred in not taking into account the devaluation of the money.
The ld. LAC should have taken note of the loss and injury suffered by the petitioner.

The ld.
LAC has grossly erred in directing the deduction of tax, from the amount of compensation of the said land as no tax from the amount of compensation and interest thereupon could be deducted.
It is stated that the petitioner has claimed the compensation for the acquire land @ Rs.2000/ per square yards in addition to Rs. 25,000/ per bigha, solatium amount along with interest.

11. Written statemnt has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/Union of India and, it is, interalia,
submitted that the petitioner is not entitled for compensation as the Delhi Land Reforms Act is applicable to the said land.

It is submitted that the land was acquired for the purposes of P.D.D.,
therefore, DDA is also a necessary party for the adjudication of the proceedings.

It is stated that the said land is not surrounded by any developed or undeveloped colony and can only be used for agriculture purpose.

It is submitted that there was no structure, tree, well or tubewell in the said land at the Sh. Narender Kumar Bindal vs Union Of India on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37672440/

sentences.text: The petitioner is not entitled for any enhancement in the compensation as they have not filed the claim in response to notice under Section 9 & 10 of the Act.
Otherwise also, the said land is in dispute with the Gaon Sabha Village and the matter is still pending, therefore, the petitioner is not entitled to any relief.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference petition filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

13. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the said land has been taken over by the DDA and as per Kabza karwahi report dated 29.11.2007 the said land has been taken back by the L&B department from DDA and handed over to DSIDC.
It is also written in Kabza Karwahi that the compensation/alternative allotment/enhanced compensation will be paid by DSIDC.
It is submitted that as the DDA is not the beneficiary of the said land, therefore, they are not liable to pay any compensation.

It is prayed that LAC no. 250/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Narender Kumar Bindal v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 11 the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.

Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?
OPP 2. Relief.
15. Matter was listed for recording of petitioners evidence.
Matter was listed for recording of petitioner's evidence.
16. Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as ld.
Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.

I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  LAC no. 250/2016 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Narender Kumar Bindal v. Union of India Page no. 8 of 11 WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?

. The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
Sh. Narender Kumar Bindal vs Union Of India on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37672440/
4

sentences.text: "The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
19. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
20. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.
LAC no. 250/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Narender Kumar Bindal v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 11 21.

entities.text: Narender Kumar Bindal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

22. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).

This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
23.
The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
LAC no. 250/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Narender Kumar Bindal v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 11 RELIEF 24.
